reliability.title: Why Adhan sounds reliably even when killed or locked
reliability.subtitle: We eliminated the classic Flutter audio-focus conflict using a three-stage native pipeline:

steps.title: Native AlarmClock Scheduling
steps.desc: Bypasses Android Doze restrictions and auto-restores 7 days of alarms after device reboots or timezone shifts.

steps.title: Isolated MediaPlayback Service
steps.desc: Holds a bounded 4-minute WakeLock with USAGE_ALARM audio focus so nothing cuts off the Adhan midway.

steps.title: Lightweight Lockscreen UI (~12MB)
steps.desc: Boots in under 50ms independently from Flutter; prepared on iOS via Time-Sensitive Alerts & SwiftUI Extension.

oems.name: Honor / Huawei (MagicOS)
steps: Disable automatic management for Zad Al-Muslim and enable Auto-launch, Secondary launch & Run in background.
In App Settings → Fix Settings, enable Lockscreen display permission.

oems.name: Xiaomi / Redmi (HyperOS)
steps: Long-press the app icon → App Info.
Enable Autostart and set Battery Saver to No Restrictions.
In Other Permissions, enable Show on Lock screen and Display pop-up windows.

oems.name: Samsung (OneUI)
steps: Open App Info → Battery → select Unrestricted.
Ensure Zad Al-Muslim is excluded from Sleeping or Deep Sleeping apps.
Verify Notifications and Alarms & Reminders permissions remain allowed.

privacyItems.why: Used purely on-device for astronomical prayer calculations, Qibla bearing, and nearby mosque search — never transmitted to tracking servers.
Required solely so the Adhan triggers at the exact second without OEM battery-saver delays.
All settings live privately on your device, and even device-matched APK routing runs ephemerally without storing device fingerprints or IP addresses.

items.q: Is Zad Al-Muslim completely free with zero ads or tracking?
items.a: Yes. It is 100% free, ad-free, and tracker-free, built as an open-source ongoing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah).

items.q: Does the Adhan ring when the phone is locked or app closed?
items.a: Yes. On Android it schedules AlarmClock triggers and plays audio from an isolated native mediaPlayback service with full lockscreen support.

items.q: Can I use Quran, Azkar, Qibla, and Prayer Times offline?
items.a: Yes. Every core worship feature works offline. Internet is only required for loading live nearby mosque map tiles.

items.q: What about the iOS / App Store version?
items.a: Current GitHub Releases distribute the Android APK directly, while native SwiftUI Lockscreen extensions and Time-Sensitive notifications are implemented for upcoming macOS/iOS builds.

items.q: Do Quran verses and Azkar stay in Arabic in English mode?
items.a: Always. All UI labels adapt to English while sacred Quranic and Prophetic texts remain in their authentic Arabic script.

downloadSection.selectArchTitle: Available Builds Guide — pick manually if downloading for another device:

arm64-v8a.label: Modern Phones
arm64-v8a.audience: Best for almost all modern Android phones since ~2017 (Samsung, Xiaomi, Honor, Oppo, Realme, Pixel) — smaller download size.

armeabi-v7a.label: Older / 32-bit Phones
armeabi-v7a.audience: Built for older Android devices or budget 32-bit phones (Android Go or pre-2017 hardware).

x86_64.label: Tablets & Emulators
x86_64.audience: Strictly for Intel/AMD Android tablets, Chromebooks, or PC Android emulators (rare on smartphones).

universal.label: Universal Build
universal.audience: Bundles every CPU type into one APK so it installs on any Android phone; ideal if unsure of processor type or sharing with others.
